findings.summary: the settlement walked every mesh carrying a `shaderVariant`, and the line and linear-depth families carry one too -- both settling their own instanced form from their options -- so a line material on a thin-instanced mesh had its `useThinInstances: false` overwritten with true while its variant name still encoded the old flags. Reproduced before fixing; only a program `createShaderMaterial` built from the entry's own WGSL is marked and settled now, with a test on the line family's flags

`thinInstances: "possible"` -- a mesh that may acquire instances from a frame callback -- was folded into "always", so the mesh took the instanced prelude whether or not the callback ran; it refuses, because the lanes are declared in the prelude the stage compiles against and the form has to be settled before the draw exists
the colour axis was OR'd silently across meshes while the instancing axis refused loudly, though the pin keys its pipeline on both (`variantKey = "" + +hasColor`); both refuse now

the refusal claimed "drawn both instanced and plain", which is not what it can detect: the flags are stamped after `reachShaderProgram` computes structural identity, so two identical `createShaderMaterial` calls collapse to one variant and the refusal could fire on two separate upstream materials neither of which is drawn both ways. It now says meshes sharing one baked variant disagree

`recordSceneMeshShaderVariant` re-implemented `recordSceneMeshMaterial`, which fires three lines away at the same site from the same Value and already writes a manifest flag out of its bag -- and the comment beside it calls that map "the one producer of the pair"; the new method, its context member and its guard are gone
the settlement threw a bare `Error`, the only scene refusal in the compiler that was not a located `CompileError`; it goes through the existing `failAtFile`

the program lookup hand-rolled a `find` over `reachedShaderPrograms` where the file exports `reachedShaderProgram`, and its `if (!program) continue` silently dropped the lanes on a state inconsistency instead of refusing

the tests hand-built `SceneMeshManifest` rows and called an exported helper, when `manifest.customShaderPrograms` already carries both flags and the file already reads them that way in three places. Rewritten through `compileSource`, which also gave the test helper's `extra` parameter -- dead, with one caller passing "" -- the refusal case to build
the `fail` callback parameter had one body used by both callers and could never take a node-attributed form, so it was not earned; it is the located `failAtFile` at the one production caller now
the lane decision walked its results twice to find the conflict; it is one pass
`nameExpression ?? object` was spelled twice in the reworked name block; hoisted to a `nameNode` that says why an absent name has no node of its own

three comments said the pin decides the lanes "never from the material", where its line is `!!ti.colors && material._tic != 0`; they now say `_tic` is a material-side opt-out this port refuses, which is why the mesh decides outright

docs/fidelity.md claimed unscoped that an instance lane's position "is the pin's, and it is taken rather than restated" -- true of the families whose fragment declares it, false of this one, which declares its own at the fixed 16-20. Both that divergence and the 21 vertex attributes it forces are written down, in fidelity.md and on the feature's own page
`corpus/babylon-lite/lab/lite/src/shared/scene66-nme.ts` came in with a sizing probe and belongs to no scene on the branch

the efficiency angle measured the whole shape rather than assuming: `reachedShaderPrograms` never exceeds 2 corpus-wide (274 of 280 scenes reach 0), the settlement costs 0.29-2.09 microseconds against compiles of 0.1-12 seconds, and the branch touches no `native/`, `src/lowering/` or `src/shader-ir.ts` file -- it flips two flags on a table the line family already built
findings.blockedBy: Nothing to apply: the measurement found no cost. The named alternatives (an early-out, and carrying the program id instead of its name) were measured at 0.29 microseconds and four string compares.
findings.filedIn: Recorded here; no TODO entry is warranted for a measurement that found no cost.

findings.summary: the deeper answer to a material drawn both ways is permutation-as-identity -- the line family already names each combination (`-ti`, `-tic`) as its own variant, so the port owns the mechanism -- rather than a refusal
findings.blockedBy: This port bakes one variant into the material record, where the pin builds a pipeline per renderable, so permutations also need the render item to pick by mesh: `bind_render_item` reads `material.shader_variant` off the material alone. That is a second variant id on the record plus a mesh-driven pick in both PALs, and no reached scene mixes the two forms.
findings.filedIn: docs/features.md, the shader-material paragraph, which names the line family's permutation convention as the shape a generalization would take.
